name: Crystagen
lead: Crystagen is a short synthetic peptide with the sequence Thr-Lys-Glu (TKE, also written EDP in some listings), one of the "Khavinson peptides" developed in Russia as so-called peptide bioregulators. It is described in the literature as an immunoprotective peptide whose reported actions concern the spleen and the immune system during ageing.[1]

The published material consists of a small number of laboratory and animal studies, largely from the St. Petersburg group that developed these peptides. A 2014 paper in a Russian gerontology journal reports that Crystagen, alongside the related peptides Vilon, Timogen and R-1, has immunoprotective effects in the ageing spleen, and that Crystagen activates B-cells.[1] No human clinical trials were found, and no study has examined it for an appearance purpose.
infobox: Research peptide; no established clinical use found

paras: Crystagen belongs to a family of very short peptides, including Vilon, Timogen and Epitalon, that researchers associated with Vladimir Khavinson propose as regulators of tissue function and ageing. It is a tripeptide made of threonine, lysine and glutamic acid.[1]

According to a 2014 review-style paper, Vilon, Timogen, Crystagen and R-1 each have immunoprotective effects in the spleen during ageing. Within that account, Vilon and R-1 are said to act on T-helper cells, Timogen on B-cells, and Crystagen is also said to activate B-cells.[1] The available text is an abstract, and the details of the experimental systems are not described here.
No studies found. The only material found is a laboratory-level report on spleen immune cells in the context of ageing.[1]

Crystagen is rarely discussed on appearance forums; its inclusion in lists of Khavinson bioregulators is tied to the immune-system claims made for that peptide family. No forum material specific to it was found.

refs.title: Molecular aspects of immunoprotective activity of peptides in spleen during the ageing process

card.summary: A Russian three-amino-acid 'bioregulator' peptide with spleen and immune claims backed only by small lab reports.
card.note: No human trials found; research-peptide status.

quick.overview:
Crystagen is a tripeptide from the Khavinson family of short peptide bioregulators, discussed in a Russian paper as an immune-supporting peptide for the ageing spleen.

The literature is small and mostly from the developing group. No human trial exists, and it has no documented role in appearance.
quick.mechanism: The cited paper reports that it activates B-cells in the spleen of ageing animals, alongside related peptides that act on T-helpers.
quick.risks: No safety data in humans was found. It is sold as a research peptide rather than an approved medicine in the sources reviewed.
